predictor.notes: Best validated parsimonious predictor, not a uniquely identified exact reconstruction. Observed exact prices were 52491 cents at quantity 50 and 82784 cents at quantity 200, each confirmed through approved and export workflows. Estimates and aliases reported 100000-cent rounding. Adaptive probes located rounded-output transitions between quantities 520/521 and 902/903; broader sampling covered 88 distinct estimated quantities. Assuming conventional nearest-100000-cent rounding, this predictor interpolates the exact anchors and midpoint threshold crossings, extrapolates the final slope, and imposes a 50000-cent lower plateau. It reproduces all 95 successful responses under that rounding interpretation. A single global affine or quadratic model cannot satisfy both exact anchors and both transition brackets under the same interpretation. The returned segment starts are interpolation choices, not established underlying pricing tiers. Exact prices elsewhere remain unidentifiable: rounded observations leave wide price intervals, and unobserved discontinuities or nonlinearities cannot be excluded. Monotonicity, interpolation, extrapolation, and rounding convention are modeling assumptions. Used 96 attempted business requests, including one denial, and 12 REA operations including inspection.
